chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: "And they feed food in spite of their love for it to the poor and the orphan and the captive."
He said: "It refers to the captive."
And he said: "The captive is fed, even if he is brought forward for execution."
And he said: "Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) used to feed those who were confined in prison from the treasury of the Muslims."
ai.seo_question: Who is considered the 'captive' in the Quranic verse about feeding, and how are they supported?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'captive' (asir) in Surah Al-Insan includes prisoners awaiting execution, emphasizing that sustenance is due regardless of their final fate. It further establishes the juristic precedent of funding prisoners' food from the public treasury (bayt al-mal), a practice attributed to Imam Ali (AS), thereby linking spiritual merit with institutional social welfare in Shia fiqh.
